requirements.title: Level-3 expressions are the character concatenation layer over level-2 expressions
requirements.definition: Level-3 expressions are level-2 expressions optionally involving concat-op. This places concatenation above relational and logical operations but below numeric level-2 syntax in the grammar ladder.
requirements.oracle:
Intrinsic character controls use fixed character literals and length checks only for admission and final value, not grouping. Grouping-sensitive future controls may instead use a non-associative defined extension of // on a derived type, with independently computed component-value oracles and valid interfaces under 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2.

requirements.title: A level-3 expression is a left-recursive chain of level-2 expressions joined by concat-op
requirements.definition: The level-3-expr syntax is either a level-2-expr or a level-3-expr followed by concat-op and level-2-expr, making unparenthesized concatenation left-recursive in the grammar.
requirements.oracle:

requirements.title: The concatenation operator token is double slash
requirements.definition: The concat-op token is '//'. It is the token used by R1011 and does not define character operand validity by itself.

pending.single-slash-not-concat: PENDING batch295: left pending because a single '/' between character operands is first a valid mult-op token and the observable rejection is operand-type interpretation, not an isolated concat-op spelling diagnostic.

requirements.oracle:
